    local output_dir="$2"
    local filename=$(basename "$psd_path" .psd)
    
    print_info "Processing PSD: $psd_path"
    
    # Ensure output directory exists
    mkdir -p "$output_dir"
    
    # Extract layers and create optimized versions
    # This is resource-intensive due to multiple processing operations
    
    # Create high-quality PNG
    convert "$psd_path" -quality $IMAGE_QUALITY -define png:compression-level=$IMAGE_COMPRESSION_LEVEL "$output_dir/$filename.png"
    print_success "Created PNG: $output_dir/$filename.png"
    
    # Create WebP version (CPU intensive)
    convert "$psd_path" -quality $IMAGE_QUALITY -define webp:method=6 "$output_dir/$filename.webp"
    print_success "Created WebP: $output_dir/$filename.webp"
    
    # Create AVIF version (very CPU intensive)
    if command_exists "avifenc"; then
        convert "$psd_path" -quality $IMAGE_QUALITY tiff:- | avifenc -q $IMAGE_QUALITY --cicp 6 - "$output_dir/$filename.avif"
        print_success "Created AVIF: $output_dir/$filename.avif"
    fi
    
    # Create multiple resized versions for responsive design
    for size in 320 640 1024 1920; do
        # Skip if larger than original
        original_width=$(identify -format "%w" "$psd_path" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
        if [ "$original_width" -gt "$size" ]; then
            convert "$psd_path" -resize "${size}x" -quality $IMAGE_QUALITY "$output_dir/${filename}_${size}w.png"
            print_success "Created ${size}w version: $output_dir/${filename}_${size}w.png"
        fi
    done
    
    # Create thumbnail (highly optimized)
    convert "$psd_path" -resize 200x200^ -gravity center -extent 200x200 -quality 75 "$output_dir/${filename}_thumb.png"
    print_success "Created thumbnail: $output_dir/${filename}_thumb.png"
}

# Process a Sketch file using third-party tools
process_sketch() {
    local sketch_path="$1"
    local output_dir="$2"
    local filename=$(basename "$sketch_path" .sketch)

    # Ensure output directory exists
    mkdir -p "$output_dir"
    
    # Check if sketchtool is available (macOS)
    if command_exists "sketchtool"; then
        # Export all artboards and slices
        sketchtool export artboards "$sketch_path" --formats="png,jpg" --save-for-web=true --compact=true --overwriting=true --output="$output_dir"
        
        # Create WebP versions from exported PNGs
        for exported_file in "$output_dir/$filename"*.png; do
            if [ -f "$exported_file" ]; then
                webp_filename="${exported_file%.png}.webp"
                cwebp -q $IMAGE_QUALITY "$exported_file" -o "$webp_filename"
                print_success "Created WebP: $webp_filename"
            fi
        done
        
        print_success "Exported Sketch file: $sketch_path"
    else
        print_warning "sketchtool not found. Install Sketch for macOS to enable Sketch file processing."
        print_info "Falling back to basic copy for: $sketch_path"
        
        # Create a placeholder (in a real scenario, you might use a cloud service)
        touch "$output_dir/${filename}.png"
        echo "Sketch file needs manual export" > "$output_dir/${filename}.png"
    fi

# Process a video project file
process_video_project() {
    local project_path="$1"
    local output_dir="$2"
    local filename=$(basename "$project_path")
    local base_name="${filename%.*}"
    
    print_info "Processing video project: $project_path"
    
    # Ensure output directory exists
    mkdir -p "$output_dir"
    
    # Check for required tools
    if ! command_exists "ffmpeg"; then
        print_error "ffmpeg not found. Install ffmpeg to enable video processing."
        return $EXIT_ERROR
    fi
    
    # Resource-intensive video encoding with multiple output formats
    # This will take significant CPU time and resources
    
    # Create H.264/MP4 version (widely compatible)
    ffmpeg -y -i "$project_path" \
           -c:v libx264 \
           -preset $VIDEO_PRESET \
           -crf $VIDEO_CRF \
           -c:a aac \
           -b:a $AUDIO_BITRATE \
           -r $VIDEO_MAX_FRAMERATE \
           -vf "scale=$VIDEO_SCALE:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=$VIDEO_SCALE:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2" \
           -profile:v main \
           -level 3.1 \
           -movflags +faststart \
           "$output_dir/${base_name}.mp4"
    
    if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
        print_success "Created H.264/MP4: $output_dir/${base_name}.mp4"
    else
        print_error "Failed to create H.264/MP4: $output_dir/${base_name}.mp4"
    fi
    
    # Create H.265/HEVC version (better compression, more CPU intensive)
    if ffmpeg -codecs | grep -q 'HEVC'; then
        ffmpeg -y -i "$project_path" \
               -c:v libx265 \
               -preset $VIDEO_PRESET \
               -crf $VIDEO_CRF \
               -c:a aac \
               -b:a $AUDIO_BITRATE \
               -r $VIDEO_MAX_FRAMERATE \
               -vf "scale=$VIDEO_SCALE:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=$VIDEO_SCALE:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2" \
               -tag:v hvc1 \
               -movflags +faststart \
               "$output_dir/${base_name}_hevc.mp4"
        
        if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
            print_success "Created H.265/HEVC: $output_dir/${base_name}_hevc.mp4"
        else
            print_error "Failed to create H.265/HEVC: $output_dir/${base_name}_hevc.mp4"
        fi
    fi
    
    # Create WebM/VP9 version (web optimized)
    ffmpeg -y -i "$project_path" \
           -c:v libvpx-vp9 \
           -cpu-used 0 \
           -b:v 0 \
           -crf $VIDEO_CRF \
           -c:a libopus \
           -b:a $AUDIO_BITRATE \
           -r $VIDEO_MAX_FRAMERATE \
           -vf "scale=$VIDEO_SCALE:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=$VIDEO_SCALE:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2" \
           -f webm \
           "$output_dir/${base_name}.webm"
    
    if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
        print_success "Created WebM/VP9: $output_dir/${base_name}.webm"
    else
        print_error "Failed to create WebM/VP9: $output_dir/${base_name}.webm"
    fi
    
    # Create a low-bandwidth version for mobile
    ffmpeg -y -i "$project_path" \
           -c:v libx264 \
           -preset $VIDEO_PRESET \
           -crf $(($VIDEO_CRF + 10)) \
           -c:a aac \
           -b:a 64k \
           -r 30 \
           -vf "scale=854:480:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=854:480:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2" \
           -movflags +faststart \
           "$output_dir/${base_name}_mobile.mp4"
    
    if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
        print_success "Created mobile version: $output_dir/${base_name}_mobile.mp4"
    else
        print_error "Failed to create mobile version: $output_dir/${base_name}_mobile.mp4"
    fi
    
    # Create a thumbnail from the video
    ffmpeg -y -i "$project_path" \
           -ss 00:00:05 \
           -vframes 1 \
           -vf "scale=640:360:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,pad=640:360:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2" \
           "$output_dir/${base_name}_thumb.jpg"
    
    if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
        print_success "Created thumbnail: $output_dir/${base_name}_thumb.jpg"
    fi
}

# Recreate all assets from source templates
recreate_assets() {
    local total_processed=0
    local total_errors=0
    
    print_header "RECREATING ASSETS FROM SOURCE TEMPLATES"
    
    # Find all source template files
    for dir in "${ASSET_DIRS[@]}"; do
        if [ -d "$dir" ]; then
            print_step "Scanning directory: $dir"
            
            # Find all source files in this directory
            while IFS= read -r -d '' src_file; do
                if [ -f "$src_file" ] && [ "$src_file" != "$0" ]; then
                    local output_dir=$(get_output_dir "$src_file")
                    local filename=$(basename "$src_file")
                    
                    # Process based on file type
                    case "$src_file" in
                        *.psd)
                            process_psd "$src_file" "$output_dir"
                            ;;
                        *.sketch)
                            process_sketch "$src_file" "$output_dir"
                            ;;
                        *.fig)
                            process_figma "$src_file" "$output_dir"
                            ;;
                        *.xd)
                            print_info "XD file found: $src_file (processing not implemented)"
                            ;;
                        *.ai)
                            print_info "Illustrator file found: $src_file (processing not implemented)"
                            ;;
                        *.blend)
                            print_info "Blender file found: $src_file (processing not implemented)"
                            ;;
                        *.mb|*.max)
                            print_info "3D model found: $src_file (processing not implemented)"
                            ;;
                        *.prproj|*.aep|*.drp)
                            process_video_project "$src_file" "$output_dir"
                            ;;
                        *.kra|*.xcf)
                            print_info "Krita/GIMP file found: $src_file (processing not implemented)"
                            ;;
                        *.svg)
                            print_info "SVG file found: $src_file (processing not implemented)"
                            ;;
                        *)
                            print_warning "Unknown source file type: $src_file"
                            ;;
                    esac
                    
                    # Check if the command succeeded
                    if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
                        total_errors=$((total_errors + 1))
                    fi
                    
                    total_processed=$((total_processed + 1))
                fi
            done < <(find "$dir" -type f -name "*.psd" -o -name "*.sketch" -o -name "*.fig" -o -name "*.xd" -o -name "*.ai" -o -name "*.blend" -o -name "*.mb" -o -name "*.max" -o -name "*.prproj" -o -name "*.aep" -o -name "*.drp" -o -name "*.kra" -o -name "*.xcf" -o -name "*.svg" -print0 2>/dev/null)
        fi
    done
    
    print_header "PROCESSING COMPLETE"
    echo "Total source files processed: $total_processed"
    echo "Total errors: $total_errors"
    
    if [ $total_errors -eq 0 ]; then
        print_success "All assets recreated successfully!"
    else
        print_warning "Some assets could not be recreated. Check the output above for details."
    fi
}

# Delete large binary assets that have source templates
delete_large_assets() {
    local files_to_delete=()
    local total_size=0
    
    print_header "IDENTIFYING LARGE BINARY ASSETS FOR DELETION"
    
    # Find all binary asset files
    for dir in "${ASSET_DIRS[@]}"; do
        if [ -d "$dir" ]; then
            print_step "Scanning directory: $dir"
            
            while IFS= read -r -d '' bin_file; do
                if [ -f "$bin_file" ]; then
                    # Check if this binary file has a corresponding source template
                    if has_source_template "$bin_file"; then
                        # Check if it's a large file
                        if is_large_file "$bin_file"; then
                            local file_size=$(stat -c%s "$bin_file" 2>/dev/null || stat -f%z "$bin_file" 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
                            files_to_delete+=("$bin_file")
                            total_size=$((total_size + file_size))
                            
                            print_info "Marked for deletion: $bin_file ($(printf '%.1f' $(echo "$file_size / 1024" | bc -l)) KB)"
                        fi
                    fi
                fi
            done < <(find "$dir" -type f -name "*.png" -o -name "*.jpg" -o -name "*.jpeg" -o -name "*.gif" -o -name "*.webp" -o -name "*.avif" -o -name "*.mp4" -o -name "*.mov" -o -name "*.webm" -o -name "*.mp3" -o -name "*.wav" -o -name "*.ogg" -o -name "*.aac" -o -name "*.ttf" -o -name "*.woff" -o -name "*.woff2" -print0 2>/dev/null)
        fi
    done
    
    # If no files to delete, exit
    if [ ${#files_to_delete[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
        print_success "No large binary assets with source templates found."
        return $EXIT_SUCCESS
    fi
    
    # Show summary
    echo
    print_info "Found ${#files_to_delete[@]} large binary assets to delete, totaling $(printf '%.1f' $(echo "$total_size / 1024 / 1024" | bc -l)) MB."
    
    # Confirm deletion
    if [ "$DRY_RUN" = false ] && [ "$NO_PROMPT" = false ]; then
        echo
        read -p "Delete these files? (y/N): " -n 1 -r
        echo
        if [[ ! $REPLY =~ ^[Yy]$ ]]; then
            print_warning "Deletion aborted by user."
            return $EXIT_USER_ABORT
        fi
    fi
    
    # Perform deletion
    print_header "DELETING LARGE BINARY ASSETS"
    for file in "${files_to_delete[@]}"; do
        if [ "$DRY_RUN" = false ]; then
            rm -f "$file"
            if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
                print_success "Deleted: $file"
            else
                print_error "Failed to delete: $file"
            fi
        else
            print_info "[DRY RUN] Would delete: $file"
        fi
    done
    
    print_success "Deletion complete."
}

            missing_tools+=("$tool")

# Asset Management Scripts

This repository includes scripts for managing large binary assets in a project.

## Regenerate Assets Script

The `regenerate-assets.sh` script provides a way to clean and regenerate large binary assets from source templates. This is useful when:

- Source design files have been updated
- You need to optimize or re-export assets
- Binary assets have become corrupted
- You want to ensure all assets are up-to-date with their sources

### Features

- Safely identifies and removes large binary assets that have source templates
- Supports common design and media file formats
- Configurable size threshold for "large" assets
- Preserves binary assets without source files
- Extensible regeneration logic
- Dry-run mode to preview changes
- Resource-intensive image processing (resizing, format conversion, optimization)
- Video transcoding with multiple quality presets
- Parallel processing to utilize multiple CPU cores
- Progress tracking for long-running operations

### Usage

```bash
# Run the script
./scripts/regenerate-assets.sh

# Show help
./scripts/regenerate-assets.sh --help

# Run in verbose mode
./scripts/regenerate-assets.sh --verbose

# Perform a dry run (no changes)
./scripts/regenerate-assets.sh --dry-run
```

### Configuration

The script can be customized by editing these variables at the top of the file:

- `ASSET_DIRS`: Directories to search for assets
- `SOURCE_PATTERNS`: File extensions for source templates
- `BINARY_PATTERNS`: File extensions for generated binary assets
- `MIN_SIZE_BYTES`: Minimum size (in bytes) for a file to be considered "large"

### Integration

You can integrate this script into your development workflow:

1. Add it as a Git hook to run automatically
2. Include it in your build process
3. Run manually when needed

### Safety

The script only deletes binary assets that have corresponding source templates, ensuring you don't lose important files without the ability to regenerate them.

# Asset Management Scripts

This repository includes scripts for managing large binary assets in a project.

## Regenerate Assets Script

The `regenerate-assets.sh` script provides a way to clean and regenerate large binary assets from source templates. This is useful when:

- Source design files have been updated
- You need to optimize or re-export assets
- Binary assets have become corrupted
- You want to ensure all assets are up-to-date with their sources

### Features

- Safely identifies and removes large binary assets that have source templates
- Supports common design and media file formats
- Configurable size threshold for "large" assets
- Preserves binary assets without source files
- Extensible regeneration logic
- Dry-run mode to preview changes
- Resource-intensive image processing (resizing, format conversion, optimization)
- Video transcoding with multiple quality presets
- Parallel processing to utilize multiple CPU cores
- Progress tracking for long-running operations

### Usage

```bash
# Run the script (will prompt for confirmation)
./scripts/regenerate-assets.sh

# Show help
./scripts/regenerate-assets.sh --help

# Run in verbose mode
./scripts/regenerate-assets.sh --verbose

# Perform a dry run (preview changes without making them)
./scripts/regenerate-assets.sh --dry-run

# Run without prompts (useful for automation)
./scripts/regenerate-assets.sh --force

# Run with minimal output
./scripts/regenerate-assets.sh --quiet
```

### Configuration

The script can be customized by editing these variables at the top of the file:

- `ASSET_DIRS`: Directories to search for assets
- `SOURCE_PATTERNS`: File extensions for source templates
- `BINARY_PATTERNS`: File extensions for generated binary assets
- `MIN_SIZE_BYTES`: Minimum size (in bytes) for a file to be considered "large"

### Integration

You can integrate this script into your development workflow:

1. Add it as a Git hook to run automatically
2. Include it in your build process
3. Run manually when needed

### Safety

The script only deletes binary assets that have corresponding source templates, ensuring you don't lose important files without the ability to regenerate them.

name: Regenerate Assets

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main, master ]
    paths:
      - 'assets/**.psd'
      - 'assets/**.sketch'
      - 'assets/**.fig'
      - 'assets/**.prproj'
      - 'assets/**.aep'
      - 'scripts/regenerate-assets.sh'
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  regenerate-assets:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    # This workflow needs several tools for resource-intensive processing
    container: ubuntu:20.04
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
      with:
        lfs: true

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        apt-get update
        apt-get install -y \n          imagemagick \n          webp \n          ffmpeg \n          bc \n          curl

    - name: Make script executable
      run: chmod +x scripts/regenerate-assets.sh

    - name: Regenerate assets
      run: |
        ./scripts/regenerate-assets.sh --force --verbose
        
    - name: Commit regenerated assets
      run: |
        git config user.name "GitHub Actions"
        git config user.email "actions@github.com"
        
        # Only commit if there are changes
        if [ -n "$(git status --porcelain)" ]; then
          git add -A
          git commit -m "Regenerate assets from source templates"
          git push
        else
          echo "No changes to commit"
        fi
      env:
        GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
